Run the eval with the `-j 1` option:

```bash
promptfoo eval -j 1
```

The docs say this "serializes the eval's **target** calls: one provider and prompt at a time." ["This serializes the eval's **target** calls: one provider and prompt at a time."] [promptfoo/site/docs/providers/ollama.md]

The same section lists two exceptions:

- Tests marked with `options.runSerially` run as a separate group before the rest, so execution order isn't strictly sequential even at `-j 1`. ["the evaluator runs test cases marked `options.runSerially` as a separate partition ahead of the rest, so a config using that option does not execute in strict test-case order even at `-j 1`."] [promptfoo/site/docs/providers/ollama.md]
- Model-graded assertions run on a separate path. If grading grouping is disabled (by a per-eval timeout or a `{{_conversation}}` variable), up to `PROMPTFOO_ASSERTIONS_MAX_CONCURRENCY` grader calls (3 by default) can still overlap within a test case. ["up to `PROMPTFOO_ASSERTIONS_MAX_CONCURRENCY` grader calls (3 by default) can still overlap within a single test case."] [promptfoo/site/docs/providers/ollama.md]

I don't have information in these documents about other ways to limit concurrency, so I can't say whether there are alternatives.
